# Worker-Task Matching with Specialties

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/worker-task-assignment)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are building a system that assigns an ordered stream of tasks to multiple workers while keeping their workloads as balanced as possible. You receive a collection of worker names and a collection of tasks, with every task containing a unique integer `id` and a positive integer `duration`.

Process the tasks in the order provided, assigning each task individually. At the time of assignment, select the worker whose current total workload—the sum of the durations of tasks already assigned to that worker—is smallest. When several workers share the smallest workload, select the one whose name comes first lexicographically.

Produce assignment strings in the form `"<task_id>:<worker_name>"`. The returned assignments may appear in any order.

## Constraints

* 1 ≤ `workers.length` ≤ 1000
* 1 ≤ `tasks.length` ≤ 1000
* 1 ≤ `duration` ≤ 1000
* Worker names are distinct, non-empty strings made only from lowercase English letters.

## Example

> **Input:**
> workers = ["alice", "bob", "carol"],
> tasks =
> [
>   { "id": 1, "duration": 4 },
>   { "id": 2, "duration": 2 },
>   { "id": 3, "duration": 7 },
>   { "id": 4, "duration": 1 }
> ]
> **Output:** ["1:alice", "2:bob", "3:carol", "4:bob"]
> **Explanation:**
> * Every worker initially has workload 0, so task 1 goes to "alice", whose name is lexicographically first.
> * For task 2, "bob" and "carol" remain at workload 0; "bob" wins the name tie-break.
> * Task 3 is given to "carol", the only worker whose workload is still 0.
> * Once the earlier tasks are assigned, "bob" has the smallest total workload for task 4, so he receives it.

## Follow-ups

Extensions the interviewer raised after the main task:

- Extend the system so that tasks have an accountId and workers remember which accounts they have helped; prefer a skilled worker who has helped that account before, choosing the least busy such worker, and fall back to the least busy skilled worker if no one has history.
- Extend the system to handle offlineEvents: a worker listed with an afterTaskIndex goes offline after that task index is assigned, cannot take new tasks, but their history is still remembered; assign remaining tasks to available workers.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Each task needs the worker with the smallest current load, so the real question is how to find that worker quickly after every assignment.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Keep the workers in a priority queue ordered by load and then by name, pop the best one, add the task duration and push the worker back.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Make sure ties on load are broken by the name ordering described in the statement, and aim for logarithmic time per task instead of scanning all workers.

</details>
